reasoning: Both attempts handle placement, players already in the game, waiting for the counts on the client, and guarding SetCore. B's runtime code is slightly better: it uses WaitForChild and its SetCore retry has a limit. However, B writes the kit attributes in the typed { "Float64": N } form, which failed the number-attribute check and doesn't match the rubric's plain JSON numbers. A's data is correct and its code works, so A wins.

criteria.criterion: StarterKit declared in a Rojo-mapped file
criteria.note: src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json with className Configuration and attributes, which builds as ReplicatedStorage.Shared.StarterKit.
"Brick": 20, "Dirt": 20, "Grass": 10, "Window": 0, "Wood": 10 are plain JSON numbers, and the build check passes.
StarterKit.server.luau is under ServerScriptService and StarterKit.client.luau is under StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit correctly and covers all types
criteria.note: findConfiguration searches ReplicatedStorage:GetDescendants() by name and class without WaitForChild, which works on the server because Rojo-built instances exist at start. It loops over BlockTypes.List, and getStartingCount warns and returns 0 for a missing or invalid value.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: It handles Players:GetPlayers() and waits on AttributeChanged until every count exists. SetCore is wrapped in pcall, but sendNotificationAsync retries with no limit.
It only adds new files, and luau-lsp, selene, StyLua and rojo build all pass.

criteria.criterion: StarterKit declared in a Rojo-mapped file
criteria.note: src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json with className Configuration, at a path the project mounts.
Uses the typed form { "Float64": 20 } instead of plain JSON numbers, and the number-attribute check failed on this file.
Edits the existing Main.server.luau and Main.client.luau, which are in the correct locations.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit correctly and covers all types
criteria.note: Uses ReplicatedStorage.Shared:WaitForChild("StarterKit"), loops over BlockTypes.List, and warns and gives 0 when a value isn't a number.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, SetCore guard
criteria.note: Handles GetPlayers(), waitForStarterKit waits on each attribute's changed signal, and SetCore is wrapped in pcall with 20 retries and a warning if they all fail.
Keeps the existing print lines and lint passes, but it fails the attribute check.

strengths: Plain number attributes that pass the build check
Validates counts: wrong type, NaN, negative, and floors fractions
Handles players already in the game, and the client waits for every count before notifying
weaknesses: SetCore retry loop has no upper limit
The descendant search on the server is more complex than needed and has no WaitForChild
Shows no notification when every count is 0

strengths: Clean WaitForChild path and a SetCore retry with a limit and a warning
Handles a kit where every count is 0 with a message
Handles players already in the game
weaknesses: Typed Float64 attribute form fails the number-attribute check and doesn't match the rubric
Adds the kit logic to Main scripts instead of separate scripts (minor)
